Aneke gave the charge during the commissioning of vehicles for the Air Warfare and Doctrine Centre, in Abuja on Tuesday, 20 October.
The Air Chief said contemporary warfare, characterised by volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity, required sound doctrines, innovative operational thinking and professional military education to prepare personnel for emerging security challenges.
The CAS, represented by the Chief of Logistics, Air Vice Marshal Henry Yurkusi, said the centre’s responsibilities in doctrinal development, research and professional military education were critical to the NAF’s institutional growth and operational readiness.
“These demands require not only capable aircraft and modern equipment but also sound doctrines, effective professional military education, informed operational planning and institutions capable of translating lessons from operations into improved combat effectiveness,” the CAS said.
Aneke said the centre’s output helped shape the Service’s understanding of air power, personnel preparation and responses to emerging operational requirements.
He described the newly commissioned vehicles as an investment in the centre’s institutional capacity, noting that they would improve mobility, the coordination of official engagements, the supervision of activities, and support for training programmes.
“Their availability is expected to reduce mobility constraints and contribute to more efficient administration,” he said.
The Air Chief, however, urged the centre’s commandant to ensure effective control, maintenance and utilisation of the vehicles, stressing that their deployment must be guided by operational priorities and strict accountability.
“Accountability and adherence to extant regulations must remain paramount,” he said.
He added that every resource entrusted to the Service should be treated as an instrument for achieving its objectives.
Aneke also urged personnel at the centre to sustain innovation and ensure their work remained relevant to the operational realities facing aircrew and ground personnel.
“We must continually assess whether our concepts, procedures and institutional approaches adequately prepare the Service for present and future challenges,” he said.
He expressed the expectation that the centre would continue producing sound doctrinal products and competent personnel capable of translating professional knowledge into operational advantage.
The CAS reaffirmed the NAF leadership’s commitment to personnel welfare, saying the administration would do its utmost to ensure personnel remained proud to serve as airmen.
He urged officers, airmen and airwomen of the centre to maintain discipline, obey the law and demonstrate compassion and humility in the discharge of their duties.
The Commandant of the AWDC, Air Vice Marshal Garba Ibrahim Jibia, said the intervention by the Chief of Air Staff had resolved longstanding mobility challenges and restored the dignity and morale of personnel.
The Commandant said personnel had faced serious difficulties commuting to and from work, while directors had lacked staff cars commensurate with their offices’ responsibilities.
“By graciously allocating vehicles to facilitate personnel movement and providing staff cars for all our directors at the Air Warfare and Doctrine Centre, you have not only resolved a logistical problem but also restored dignity, morale and pride to deserving officers and men of the Nigerian Air Force,” he said.
Jibia described the intervention as evidence of Aneke’s commitment to personnel welfare, which he said was central to the Air Chief’s command philosophy.
Beyond the welfare intervention, Jibia said the centre was strengthening its role in developing air power doctrines, coordinating military exercises and supporting joint operations involving the Armed Forces of Nigeria.
He said the centre had been given the additional responsibility of coordinating air-ground integration and civilian harm mitigation in ongoing counterterrorism and counterinsurgency operations.
According to him, the expanded mandate is intended to improve cooperation between air and ground forces and strengthen the conduct of military operations.
The commandant said his focus since assuming command on 6 January 2026 had been to facilitate the seamless integration of air, land and maritime forces through doctrines that reflected prevailing operational realities.
“Our focus … has remained: to facilitate seamless integration of air, land and maritime forces in a joint environment, using dynamic air power doctrines that reflect prevailing operational realities,” he said.
He pledged that the newly provided vehicles would be properly maintained and deployed strictly for the purpose of improving operational efficiency and service delivery.
“We assure you that these vehicles will be well maintained, properly utilised and deployed strictly to enhance operational efficiency and service delivery in line with our mandate and your command philosophy,” he said.
